title: Sky Governance retains a Risk-Capital override that can re-enable PATTERN emissions despite them being 'permanently disabled'
content:
The same provision that seals PATTERN's supply immediately reopens it for one actor. A.6.1.1.6.2.1.4.2.1.1.6: "Sky Governance retains the ability to revert where Pattern is in violation of Risk Capital requirements and emissions are required by the Risk Framework."

There is a genuine tension on the face of the text: emissions are called *permanently* disabled and yet a named authority can revert them. The resolution is that "permanent" is scoped to Pattern's own governance layer, not to the system as a whole — which means the word is doing less work than it appears to, and a reader who stops at the first clause will misjudge the guarantee.

The carve-out is tightly conditioned by a **conjunction**: Pattern must be in violation of Risk Capital requirements *and* the Risk Framework must require emissions. Neither a Pattern funding shortfall alone nor a general Sky Governance preference is sufficient. That structure makes dilution a solvency remedy rather than a policy lever.

The economic reading is that PATTERN holders are implicitly the residual absorbers of Pattern's risk failures: if the Agent breaches its capital requirements, the repair mechanism issues claims against them. Non-dilution therefore holds precisely in the states of the world where the Agent is healthy, and lapses in the states where holders would most want it — an asymmetry worth understanding before treating the cap as a hard supply guarantee.
description: The exception fires only where Pattern violates Risk Capital requirements and the Risk Framework requires issuance, making the Agent's token supply a recapitalization resource of last resort.
